newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian stocks to take cue from petrol price hike.
newsitem.headline: Indian stocks to take cue from petrol price hike.

text.p: Indian blue chips are expected to drift lower this week on an anticipated rise in government-set oil prices, analysts and dealers said.
A policy-making body of India's 15-party minority coalition was scheduled to meet on Sunday to decide about domestic prices of oil, which India imports and sells below world prices.
The announcement of poor annual results by leading companies in 1997/98 (April- March) will add to a bearish market sentiment, dealers said.

"There is hardly any scope for the markets to go up," said Amit Shah, institutional sales dealer at brokerage P.R. Subramaniam. "With the looming fear of a petrol price hike, one should take a short-term bearish view."
Top government officials have warned about an increase in oil prices, but the inability to come up with a decision fast has worried market players.
"The major hurdle is the official announcement of the hike and the form in which the oil increase will be decided," said Kirit Vora, senior analyst at Nucleus Securities.

The widening gap between India's oil demand and domestic supplies called for a 20-25 percent increase, but political pressures might force the government to restrict the increase for kerosene, analysts said.
Leftist members of the government are opposed to any reduction in the kerosene subsidy, fearing it would affect their popularity with voters.
Kerosene is the basic cooking and lighting fuel for about 300 million poor Indians.
"It seems that the government does not have the political courage to come up with drastic measures," Nucleus's Vora said.
Poor earnings announcements last week by Tata Iron & Steel Ltd (TISCO), India's largest private sector steel maker, and tobacco conglomerate ITC Ltd will dampen sentiment, analysts said.
"There is nothing really exciting in the market," said Subramaniam's Shah.
Truck-maker Tata Engineering & Locomotive Company (TELCO), engineering firm Larsen & Toubro and multinational Colgate Palmolive are due to announce annual results for fiscal 1996/97 this week.
"It is going to be another round of fence-sitting. People should just stay invested in top blue chips," said Nucleus's Vora.
